minutes.headline: Task force edited the wording of a non-binding advisory vote on a stormwater utility fee versus the operating budget; no formal votes.
minutes.summary: The Stormwater Task Force spent the meeting line-editing the warrant article and summary for a non-binding advisory town meeting vote choosing between a stormwater enterprise fund/utility fee and funding through the operating budget. Members debated how to phrase the likelihood of an override, whether to cite the statute, and how to describe flat residential and impervious-area fees. No formal motions were recorded; a presentation and legal review by town counsel were planned.

budget_items.topic: Engineer position under operating budget versus utility
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said it was unclear whether the engineer position would remain if funded through the operating budget, and that outsourcing amounts need firming up.
A member said an override calculator put the increase for the average home near the utility fee range.
Members said the fee is coming in around the low 80s per household, and was raised slightly to allow for abatements reducing revenue.
A member said the stormwater need would add to what every other town department is requesting.
A member recalled a resident worrying about a large annual bill given impervious area.
Members chose not to put a tentative amount in the article, sticking with the promised cap while noting a likely range.

decisions.decision: Reworded the summary's directive sentence; the final sentence was deleted.
Agreed to keep 'will likely require' override wording and delete the last sentence of the summary.
Agreed to remove the 'under the provisions of Proposition 2 and a half' phrase from option two.
Agreed to hold off on a tentative fee amount and keep the 'less than $100' language.
Agreed to have Tim add the presentation item to the next agenda.
Agreed to send the agreed draft to town counsel Adam Costa for review.

what_happened.line: The Stormwater Task Force took no formal votes; it spent the meeting editing the warrant article and summary for a non-binding advisory town meeting vote.
The advisory question asks town meeting to choose between a stormwater utility fee and funding through the operating budget.
Members agreed to keep the 'will likely require' override wording, delete the summary's last sentence, and drop the Proposition 2 and a half phrase from option two.
Members chose not to put a tentative fee amount in the article and kept the 'less than an amount as heard ' language.
The agreed draft is to go to town counsel for review, and a presentation item is to be added to the next agenda.

why_it_matters: The wording of this advisory question shapes how residents are asked to weigh a stormwater utility fee, billed per household, against paying for stormwater through the operating budget, which members said would likely need a tax override.
The vote is non-binding, but it will signal which way the town leans on funding stormwater compliance, and members said the need would also add to what other town departments are requesting.
